controls.label: Thermal glow
controls.qualification: Black-body colour at its measured dayside temperature, 1,010 K. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The colour of TrES-1 b's heat: a black body at the dayside brightness temperature measured in secondary eclipse at 4.5 µm (Spitzer Space Telescope satellite Infrared Array Camera (IRAC)). Its star lights the day side; the night side is not measured. Reflected starlight is not included.

charts.alt: The orbits of TrES-1's planets in this map from above, to scale, with TrES-1 b highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

TrES-1 b's dayside emission: the light lost as the planet passes behind its star: its day side's own glow and reflected light. 4 measured bins from Cubillos et al. 2014 (Spitzer Space Telescope satellite, Infrared Array Camera (IRAC)), as the NASA Exoplanet Archive lists them. Horizontal bars are wavelength bins; vertical bars are the published 1-sigma errors.

TrES-1 b crossing its star, as TESS recorded it: 3 sectors (74, 80, 81) of the SPOC pipeline's 2-minute light curves of TIC 120757718, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, then averaged in 10-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.

physical.credit: Radius from Stassun et al. 2017 (2017AJ....153..136S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive; mass from Stassun et al. 2017, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2017AJ....153..136S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive; orbit from Stassun et al. 2017 (2017AJ....153..136S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive
